selection.reason: Japan's largest civilian manufacturer, with a sourced French plant (TMMF, Valenciennes) that links the pilot's two countries, and the maker of the JGSDF High Mobility Vehicle. The game's sourced 1990 lean-production technology for Japan names the Toyota Production System, so this dossier extends an existing reference.

existing_game_references.note: Evidence text names the Toyota Production System.

summary: Toyota Motor Corporation (formed by the 1982 merger of Toyota Motor Company and Toyota Motor Sales) kept its name through the window. It reorganised its European operations in 1990, completed its first UK car in 1992, launched the Prius in 1997, made Daihatsu (1998) and Hino (2001) consolidated subsidiaries, started Yaris production in France in 2001, made Daihatsu wholly owned in 2016 and took full ownership of the Czech Kolin plant in 2021. Hino left the consolidated group on 1 April 2026. Toyota also makes the JGSDF High Mobility Vehicle and 1½-ton truck.

proposed.uncertainty: The existing 1990 evidence cites the Toyota Production System; the link is identity only and grants no mechanic.
Cars have no product consumer; a real identity would replace one generated manufacturing contractor, not add a firm with sales.

duplicates_avoided: Toyota Industries (forklifts since the 2001 transfer), Daihatsu, Hino and other Toyota Group companies are separate legal persons; their products are not Toyota Motor Corporation products.
Nissan (the Renault alliance partner in fr_renault) and Mitsubishi Motors are separate carmakers not researched here.
The Hino and Mitsubishi Fuso integration is not a Toyota merger.

integration_flow.summary: A later, reviewed integration could attach this sourced identity to a company created through the existing orders. Design stays with the commissioning country; Defense R&D pays development as work is performed; the company funds tooling, national-warehouse inputs and fabrication from its own settled cash; the buyer purchases whole finished units from company stock; delivery follows fiscal settlement and seven accessible days. No company order builds civilian cars or soft-skinned military trucks; a Toyota identity would first appear only as a sector contractor serving funded work.

steps.note: Paid capitalisation from Defense procurement (political capital price applies); leases one existing completed Arms Plant slot. No historical factory, balance or stock is granted.
Further paid working capital; unsettled receivables are not spendable cash.
Frozen design revision; Defense R&D pays engineering, prototype and trials work day by day; prototypes are never saleable.
Finite company-owned stock target (0-12 units); a target is never a government order.
Government buys whole units from existing company stock; settlement then seven accessible delivery days.

unmapped: Passenger cars, hybrids and fuel-cell vehicles: no civilian product consumer.
High Mobility Vehicle and 1½-ton truck: unarmoured utility vehicles; no designer platform or kit represents soft-skinned transport.
Overseas plants: no company-to-company ownership or foreign plant model exists.

gaps: An old JGSDF vehicles address answered HTTP 403 to a single untimed pre-check; the current page was used, so no inaccessible record is claimed.
The name of the Hino-Mitsubishi Fuso holding company (ARCHION) is known only from news leads.
NUMMI and the 2002 PSA joint-venture formation appear in the Japanese securities report but are recorded only through the Toyota Europe newsroom (TPCA, 2021).

future_policy.note: Nothing after the frozen cutoff is predicted. Any later product, successor or business in a campaign must be authored as explicitly fictional game content (labelled "(fictional)") or left unknown.
